title: Directional Gradient Projection for Robust Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models

contributions.purpose: Improve robust fine-tuning of foundation models, avoiding the underfitting and heavy hyper-parameter tuning of prior magnitude-based weight-projection methods that ignore gradient direction.
contributions.mechanism: Directional Gradient Projection (DiGraP): a layer-wise trainable method reframing robust fine-tuning as multi-objective optimization (task loss + L2-SP regularization). When the two objectives' gradient directions conflict (opposite), it projects one gradient onto the orthogonal direction of the other; a trainable directional projection strength omega in [0,1] dynamically learns the priority between objectives.
contributions.evaluation: DiGraP consistently outperforms existing baselines across image classification and VQA tasks with both discriminative and generative backbones, improving both ID generalization and OOD robustness (SOTA ID and OOD).
contributions.domain: Robust fine-tuning of foundation models (vision / vision-language)
contributions.source_quote: We propose a layer-wise trainable directional gradient projection method DiGraP for robust fine-tuning of large foundation models with the intuition of bridging regularization and multi-objective optimization. This is the first robust fine-tuning methods that considers the directional information of the gradients.

contributions.purpose: Extend robust fine-tuning evaluation, previously limited to uni-modal settings, to multi-modal (VQA) settings with a principled OOD categorization.
contributions.mechanism: Construct new evaluation settings: an Image-Classification-reformulated VQA benchmark bridging uni-modal and multi-modal, plus categorization of ten OOD VQA datasets into ID / near-OOD / far-OOD by distribution-shift type and degree (uni-modal, multi-modal, adversarial).
contributions.evaluation: Provides a consistent comparative analysis of robust fine-tuning algorithms across the ten categorized VQA datasets; qualitative benchmark/setting contribution used to evaluate all methods.
contributions.domain: Robust fine-tuning evaluation for VQA / vision-language
contributions.source_quote: We propose new settings for evaluating robust fine-tuning of VQA. We first conduct experiments on Image Classification reformulated VQA benchmarks. We then categorize the existing OOD VQA datasets into different types and degrees of distribution shifts and present a consistent comparative analysis of robust fine-tuning algorithms.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate DiGraP's consistent superiority across modalities and both robustness axes.
contributions.mechanism: Comparative experiments against robust fine-tuning baselines on uni-modal and multi-modal tasks, measuring ID generalization and OOD robustness.
contributions.evaluation: DiGraP consistently outperforms other baselines across uni-modal and multi-modal tasks in both ID generalization and OOD robustness.
contributions.domain: Robust fine-tuning of foundation models (vision / vision-language)
contributions.source_quote: We show that DiGraP consistently outperforms other baselines across uni-modal and multi-modal tasks in both ID generalization and OOD robustness.

self_declared_provenance.quote: TPGM (Tian et al., 2023a) and FTP (Tian et al., 2023b) consider the regularization term as the constraint to reformulate the problem from a bi-level optimization prospective and propose to learn different hard constraints for each layer. However, these methods are computationally heavy and often apply overly strong constraints which results in underfitting ... these methods perform weight projection ... which is magnitude-wise but does not encode any directional information. This motivates us to think of direction-based methods.

L2-SP (Li et al., 2018) imposes a regularization term on the distance between the fine-tuned and pre-trained weights. ... We re-examine the regularization problem from a multi-objective optimization perspective and propose Directional Gradient Projection (DiGraP).

Agrawal et al. (2023) conducts cross-dataset evaluations with four VQA datasets, while Ma et al. (2024) and Li et al. (2021) provides a more comprehensive and detailed robustness analysis ... We build on these efforts by introducing further granularity with near and far OOD distinctions and measuring the distance between distributions.

notes: Positive results throughout; DiGraP claims SOTA on both ID and OOD across image classification and VQA. Explicit contrast/critique of prior work (TPGM/FTP cause underfitting and are compute-heavy) is a motivation rather than a negative result for the proposed method. C2 is a resource/benchmark-setting contribution (VQA OOD categorization); C1 is the core method. No negative or trade-off result reported for DiGraP.
